note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  • Progressive numbness, tingling, and subjective weakness of left arm (elbow to hand) × 2 weeks.  • Occasional shoulder discomfort with movement.  • One transient episode of left-eye visual field loss (~20 min) a few weeks ago.  • Recent viral-type illness with fatigue and headaches.  • No known hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular disease.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Father – hypothyroidism, unspecified autoimmune disease; Mother – type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Ibuprofen PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented); vitamin D (dose/frequency not documented); iron supplement intermittently (dose/frequency not documented); melatonin PRN (dose/frequency not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Physically active; recently started boxing classes.  Occasional binge alcohol use (episode of heavy drinking noted); no data on tobacco, illicit drugs, or diet.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Transient left-eye visual loss episode; does not use corrective lenses; no hearing issues reported.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Concerned/anxious about current neurologic symptoms; no depression or self-harm ideation reported.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  Works full-time (details not recorded); no other social determinants documented.  

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded.  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Not recorded.  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Not recorded.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not recorded.  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded.  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Progressive unilateral upper-limb paraesthesia/weakness (digits 2-4 palmar distribution, extending to elbow) unrelieved by conservative measures.  
• Transient monocular visual disturbance.  
• Recent viral illness; physically active 46-year-old woman.  
• Family history of autoimmune disease.

Working diagnosis  
• Suspected demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis) – supported by separate neurologic events (visual disturbance + focal sensory deficit), typical demographic, and clinician concern.

Supporting differentials (consistent with DDx)  
• Cervical radiculopathy (C6/C7) – repetitive neck/shoulder strain from boxing; dermatomal distribution possible but lacks neck pain.  
• Median nerve entrapment – palmar digits 2-4 involvement; proximal symptoms lessen likelihood.

Plan  
• Urgent neurology referral for definitive assessment.  
• Anticipate MRI brain and cervical spine ± contrast, visual evoked potentials, and baseline bloods.  
• Educated patient on red-flag symptoms (worsening weakness, visual loss, headache, vomiting, seizures) and advised immediate ED presentation if occur.  
• No disease-specific pharmacotherapy initiated pending specialist review.  
• Continue symptomatic use of ibuprofen if needed.  
• Encourage activity modification (pause boxing) until diagnosis clarified.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed importance of moderating alcohol binges and balancing exercise with rest; further counselling deferred until after neurologic evaluation.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Wants explanation of arm numbness and prevention of disability.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Neurology referral arranged; no other referrals documented.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Follow-up after neurology assessment; advised earlier review if symptom progression.  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  mental_health_support_or_not_recorded  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Neurology referral initiated (documented).  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  dental_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Consider optometry/ophthalmology if recurrent visual symptoms.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  audiometry_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  social_support_referral_or_not_recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Multiple sclerosis – Medium likelihood: transient visual loss + evolving unilateral sensory deficit in 46-year-old woman, post-viral history, autoimmune family background.  
2. Cervical radiculopathy (C7) – Medium likelihood: limb distribution and onset after repetitive boxing activity suggest mechanical nerve root irritation.  
3. Median nerve entrapment – Low-Medium likelihood: palmar 2-4 digit symptoms fit CTS, but proximal arm involvement makes isolated peripheral entrapment less probable.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals, BMI, immunisation status, smoking status, comprehensive neuro exam, blood work, chronic disease screening.  
● Internal conflicts/contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; telehealth setting limited physical examination and vitals.
